newsitem.title: USA: Medco Research drug voted down by FDA panel.
newsitem.headline: Medco Research drug voted down by FDA panel.

text.p: Medco Research Inc said Thursday a Food and Drug Administration panel voted not to recommend approval of Medco's Bidil drug for the treatment of congestive heart failure.
The action of the Cardio-Renal Advisory Committee, by a vote of eight to three, is not binding on the FDA, the company said.
A New Drug Application (NDA) for Bidil -- a combination of hydralazine hydrochloride and isosorbide dinitrate -- was filed in July 1996.
Medco said it made the application based on two landmark trials previously conducted by Veterans Administration cooperative study groups.

"We are surprised at today's outcome, given that the medical community has already adopted this combination in congestive heart failure practice guidelines worldwide," said Roger Blevins, Medco president.

"We have not yet had time to deliberate on the proceedings or outcome of this meeting, and our plans for Bidil will certainly depend upon whether we believe the specific concerns of the committee...are surmountable at a reasonable continued investment by the company," he said.
The panel's action is a set-back for the Bidil effort, but the company's portfolio of development drugs remains focused on adenosine and cardiac imaging, he said.
Medco is a pharmaceutical company engaged in the global commercialization of cardiovascular medicines and adenosine-based products.
